title: Design Hotel & Property Booking (Airbnb)
subtitle: Geospatial search, date-range availability bitmasks, and double-booking prevention

stages.title: Stage 1 — Basic Relational Property Search
stages.bottleneck: SQL queries checking date availability (`WHERE checkin >= X AND checkout <= Y`) scan millions of rows, locking the DB under search spikes.
stages.narrative:
**Monolithic Date-Range Queries.** Search requests execute a heavy `JOIN` between listings and bookings tables to check if dates overlap.

**Bottleneck:** High latency (>1s) and database locks during peak holiday search spikes.

stages.title: Stage 2 — Date-Range Availability Bitmaps & Redis Cache
stages.bottleneck: Searching 10M listings across 365 calendar days requires fast bitwise date checks.
stages.narrative: **Bitwise Availability Indexing.** Each listing represents 365 calendar days as a 365-bit vector in Redis (`0` = booked, `1` = available). Checking 7-day availability executes a single bitwise `AND` operation in sub-millisecond time.

stages.title: Stage 3 — Distributed Reservation Locks (Saga Pattern)
stages.bottleneck: Two guests trying to book the exact same apartment for the same dates at the same second.
stages.narrative: **Double-Booking Prevention.** When a guest clicks 'Reserve', an atomic Redis hold (`SETNX listing_id:date_range user_id EX 900`) grants a 15-minute temporary reservation lock. If payment succeeds, the hold turns into a confirmed DB booking.

stages.title: Stage 4 — Global Search & Dynamic Pricing Engine
stages.bottleneck: Prices fluctuate based on seasonality, local events, and demand spikes. Elasticsearch needed for complex category filters.
stages.narrative: **Elasticsearch & Dynamic Pricing.** Search attributes ('Pool', 'Pet friendly', 'Beachfront') are indexed in Elasticsearch. The Dynamic Pricing Engine applies ML demand models to suggest optimized rates to hosts in real-time.
